cards.explanation: The answer is that everyone praises Him. Luke 4:15 says He taught in their synagogues and “…was glorified by everyone.” Everyone, friends. The news about Him had spread throughout the surrounding region too. I can't even get a whole family to agree on one cookie shape, so that's a big deal.
The answer is Nazareth. Luke 4:16 says it plainly: “Then Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up.” This is His hometown. Keep that in mind for what comes next.

The answer is True. Luke 4:16 says, “As was His custom, He entered the synagogue on the Sabbath.” That word custom means it's a habit, not a one-time visit. Some people have a favorite chair at church. Jesus has a routine here too.

The answer is Isaiah. Luke 4:17 says “…the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him.” Isaiah was a prophet of God. Jesus unrolls the scroll and finds the exact place He wants. No searching around like I do for the right mixing bowl.

The answer is the blind. The reading says He has sent Me to proclaim “…recovery of sight to the blind…” It's right there in Luke 4:18. So the poor are to hear good news, and the blind are to hear a proclamation of recovery of sight. That list is longer than my cookie order on a holiday.

The answer is False. Luke 4:20 says, “The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on Him…” Everyone is watching, not wandering off, friends. I think a room with every eye on Him is waiting to hear what He says next.

The answer is that it is fulfilled today. He begins by saying, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.” (Luke 4:21) Today, right there in the room. He doesn't say it's coming later. He says this is happening while they listen.

The answer is Joseph. The crowd asks, “Isn’t this the son of Joseph?” (Luke 4:22) They ask whose son He is, and Joseph is the name they give. Right before that, all spoke well of Him and marveled at the gracious words that came from His lips.

The answer is Capernaum. Jesus says they'll tell Him, “Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.” (Luke 4:23) Capernaum is the town Jesus names there. In that saying, the ask is to do those same things in His hometown.

The answer is that he is not accepted there. Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.” (Luke 4:24) A prophet can be known and loved in one place and still not accepted at home. I think that stings, friends. Home is where you want a good reception.

The answer is False. Jesus is talking about Elijah, the prophet. He says, “Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.” (Luke 4:26) Many widows in Israel, and Elijah wasn't sent to any of them. He was sent somewhere else.
The answer is Zarephath in Sidon. Jesus says Elijah was sent “…to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.” (Luke 4:26) So he wasn't sent to a widow in Israel at all. Zarephath in Sidon is where he was sent.

The answer is Naaman. Jesus says there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, “Yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.” (Luke 4:27) Naaman is the one Jesus names. Not one of those lepers in Israel was cleansed, and He names a Syrian instead.

The answer is True. Luke 4:28 says, “On hearing this, all the people in the synagogue were enraged.” All of them, friends. It's a heavy turn. Earlier in the passage, they were speaking well of Him (Luke 4:22).

The answer is to throw Him over the cliff. Luke 4:29 says they led Him to the brow of the hill “…in order to throw Him over the cliff.” It's a hard thing to read, and I think it hurts. It's the same crowd from just a few verses earlier.

The answer is False. Luke 4:30 says, “But Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way.” They led Him to the edge to throw Him, but they don't do it. He passes through the crowd and keeps going.
